_about: Deductions from the fit score for findings in reviews that clash with the buyer's criteria (75/77-inch OLED or Mini LED, picture quality first: real local dimming, high brightness, native 100 Hz or more). Points are negative. Shown in the fit breakdown on the Ranking and model pages.

75QNED83B.reason: likely edge-lit despite the Mini LED label (third-party spec listings, 2025 predecessor tier)

75QNED87A.reason: edge-lit per John Lewis and the RTINGS-tested US sibling; heavy haloing

75QNED87B.reason: backlight type unverified; the predecessor tier was edge-lit

75QNED8M.reason: dimming tier unspecified; the 2026 QNED85 sibling is listed as edge-lit

75M80H.reason: no local dimming at all on the 65-inch (RTINGS)

75LS03F.reason: edge-lit Mini LED and extra lag through the wireless One Connect box

75LS03HW.reason: edge-lit with few zones and 32 ms+ lag through the wireless box

75W95A.reason: local dimming switches off when VRR is on (RTINGS)

75W95B.reason: local dimming switches off when VRR is on (choose.tv)

75UR9S.reason: input lag above 30 ms with local dimming on in one lab test

75P8L.reason: only about 60 to 72 dimming zones and 450 nits on the 65-inch: near-absent local dimming (What Hi-Fi, AVPasion)

75RM7L.reason: some datasheets list a 100 Hz native panel with 144 Hz only in game mode; unverified

75QNED866RE.reason: IPS-type panel with about 180 zones: low contrast and haloing

75U8HQ.reason: European units use an IPS panel with 160 to 180 zones (What Hi-Fi: poor backlighting)

75U8Q.reason: sources disagree on whether the 75-inch uses a VA or an ADS-Pro (IPS-type) panel, which would cost contrast

XIAOMI TV S MINI LED 75.reason: owners report VRR resetting after power-off on PS5

77S90D.reason: panel supplier varies by size and the 77-inch is reported as W-OLED rather than QD-OLED

XR77A80L.reason: only two full HDMI 2.1 inputs and a dim panel by current standards

XR77A95L.reason: two HDMI 2.1 inputs on European units, one shared with eARC
